title: California commits US$30 million to quantum research as Newsom signs fusion legislation
key_facts: Governor Gavin Newsom announced US$30 million for quantum and deep-space research at a UC Berkeley quantum laboratory
Money supports research, public-private partnerships and start-ups, building on the Quantum California initiative launched in 2025
Newsom signed SB 925, requiring a statewide fusion strategy, and AB 2647, calling for an assessment of new nuclear and advanced nuclear technologies
California is working toward 100% zero-carbon electricity by 2045
State hosts the DIII-D fusion facility and Lawrence Livermore's National Ignition Facility
Article is short and gives no breakdown of the $30 million
quote_evidence: California has moved to turn its quantum and fusion research base into an industrial advantage.
SB 925 requires a statewide fusion strategy covering research, commercialisation, manufacturing and regulatory planning.
why_it_matters_hint: State money for quantum research, alongside fusion laws that mostly require plans and assessments.
notes: No breakdown of funding given; one outlet read.
